headline: Hit by a Car, a Fox Named Chance Swims Toward Recovery
meta_description: A fox cub struck by a car is making a miraculous recovery thanks to swimming therapy at a canine centre in Mansfield, England.
summary_short: A fox cub left for dead after being hit by a car is regaining strength through hydrotherapy sessions at a dog rehabilitation centre.
body:
A young fox named Chance, left for dead after being struck by a car in Nottinghamshire last June, is making a remarkable recovery thanks to an unexpected rehabilitation program: hydrotherapy swimming sessions. When first discovered, the injured kit's back legs were completely non-functional, and a veterinarian feared euthanasia would be necessary. Wildlife rescuers instead took him into their care and enrolled him in assisted swims at the Mansfield Canine Centre, where his caretaker Chelsea guides him through the water. The low-impact treatment, normally used for recovering dogs, has proven transformative. Chance is now using his back legs to support himself, regaining sensation, and kicking actively in the water.

What makes Chance's story remarkable is not just the recovery itself, but the quiet dedication behind it. To preserve his wild instincts and maximize his chances of eventual release, human contact has been deliberately minimized throughout treatment. Cathy Fraser, who works at the canine centre, describes witnessing the transformation as "an incredible journey." The staff hope that if his progress continues, Chance will one day be released back into the English countryside where he belongs.

Behind this individual success lies a broader concern. Mansfield Wildlife Rescue has reported a worrying surge in vehicle strikes involving foxes, with five injured foxes treated by the centre this year alone. The cause, according to rescue founder Cheryl Martins, traces to extreme heat driving rodents into hiding, forcing hungry foxes to venture into towns and busier roads in search of food. Chance's survival and recovery offer hope—and a reminder that compassion and science, working together, can sometimes turn tragedy into a second chance.
quick_facts: Fox cub named Chance hit by car in Nottinghamshire, England, June
Paralyzed back legs treated via hydrotherapy at Mansfield Canine Centre
Five vehicle-struck foxes rescued by centre in one year
Extreme heat drives foxes into towns searching for food
